description: A bind-mounted config whose content hash is not on the service's labels won't recreate the container on edit — must be flagged. The input is the Pi package's alloy service with its `homelab.config-sha256` label stripped.
input:
Review this proposed edit to a daniel-pi Compose service:
```yaml
# hosts/components/pi-compose/services/alloy/compose.yaml.j2 (proposed)
services:
  alloy:
    volumes:
      - type: bind
        source: /usr/lib/homelab/compose/alloy/config.alloy
        target: /etc/alloy/config.alloy
        read_only: true
    labels:
      - "autokuma.alloy.enabled=false"
```
Context: config.alloy is a plain package file installed beside the compose file and bind-mounted read-only, and Alloy reads its config once, at startup. The Pi's package applies the project with `docker compose up -d`, which recreates a container only when its compose definition changes; Compose cannot see the content of a bind-mounted file. The live template carries the label `homelab.config-sha256={{ alloy_config_sha256 }}`, the sha256 of the rendered config.alloy, so a config edit changes the definition and `up -d` recreates the container. The edit drops that label. Everything you need is above. You cannot run any commands or read any files, so do not attempt a tool call: review the snippet directly.
rubric: PASS only if the review flags that dropping the homelab.config-sha256 label means an edit to config.alloy no longer changes the compose definition, so `up -d` will NOT recreate the container and the change sits inert on disk while the deploy reports green, and recommends restoring the label carrying the rendered config's hash.
